entities.name: Thin-strut porcine stent response
observations: In normal pig coronaries at one month, a 65-µm CoCr stent with fixed geometry, uniform cells, and improved surface finish had lower stenosis (2±1% vs 17±5%), intimal thickness (0.11±0.01 vs 0.23±0.03 mm), and histologic area stenosis (19±2% vs 32±3%) than a 91-µm cobalt-alloy BMS; injury was similarly low and endothelialization complete.

entities.name: Polyzene-F porcine stent response
observations: A 71-µm CoCr stent with nano-thin Polyzene-F coating reduced neointimal thickness versus bare metal at 28 and 90 days; endothelial coverage was similar, while inflammation reductions were not statistically significant.

entities.name: Design response is not uniform
observations: Polymer-free drug-eluting stent effects on endothelialization and neointimal growth varied by drug and dose; some comparative design studies also found greater thrombogenicity or slower healing with other designs. Overall response depends on platform and formulation.
